mappedContracts.statement: No requirement may be removed, weakened, deferred, or reinterpreted silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Any exception contains the affected contract IDs, evidence, risk, compensating controls, expiry, owner, and explicit user approval.
Contract changes produce a new contract version and plan hash.
Codex chooses a safe best-effort implementation rather than asking avoidable clarification questions.
requiredEvidence: ADR or decision record for material changes

mappedContracts.statement: Maintain an evidence-backed threat model for CLI, browser, internal API, official API, MCP stdio, MCP HTTP, registry distribution, state storage, and supply-chain boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Threats include credential exfiltration, SSRF, prompt/argument injection, path traversal, confused deputy, replay, duplicate mutation, supply-chain compromise, PII leakage, and malicious repository content.
Each threat maps to controls, tests, residual risk, and owner.
The model is reviewed for each release.

mappedContracts.statement: Provide predictable machine and human CLI modes, contextual completions, stable exit codes, cancellation, timeouts, config explain, and accessible help.
acceptanceCriteria: Commands support JSON/JSONL where appropriate, --quiet, --no-color, --output, and documented exit codes.
Bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell completions are contextual and tested.

mappedContracts.statement: Generate README feature tables, command documentation, MCP catalogues, schemas, safety classifications, support matrix, and roadmap status from executable sources of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: No stale version, capability, quality, or completion claim remains.
Lifecycle labels distinguish planned, implemented, contract-verified, simulator-verified, canary-verified, production-observed, and deprecated.

mappedContracts.statement: Mature repository context for Codex and other agents using concise canonical AGENTS guidance, ADRs, architecture maps, data classifications, invariants, runbooks, and generated context indexes.
acceptanceCriteria: Context is layered and avoids duplicated, contradictory instructions.
High-risk invariants are available near relevant code.
